acceptance_criteria: ciet_v2_opcua_client, UNMODIFIED, discovers and drives the v3 simulator; node ids that v2 defined retain their meaning; the module still builds headless for aarch64-linux-android.
description:
Maintainer requirement: 'opcua server capabilities that should fit the existing opcua client'. Read literally - the bundled client must work against v3 WITHOUT being modified.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (2,965 lines, verified 2026-08-13) - this is a contract-compatibility job, not a from-scratch server:
  src/opcua_core/  - reactor-AGNOSTIC half: TCP transport, server thread + tokio runtime, PKI paths, mDNS discovery, address-space construction, read/write callbacks. Its own docs say it serves ANY OUTRAM PARK simulator. DO NOT rewrite this.
  src/ciet_opcua/  - CIET's half: state.rs (707), node_map.rs (746), simulator.rs (588), pki_paths.rs (200), server.rs (184), discovery.rs (71), user_controls.rs, mod.rs. Its header explicitly names it 'the shared interface between the two CIET v2 binaries'.
  src/bin/ciet_v2_opcua_client/ - the client that must keep working.

THE ACTUAL WORK is deciding how v3 relates to ciet_opcua's node map: either v3 populates the SAME node map (client works untouched, which is the stated requirement), or the node map gains v3 variables ADDITIVELY so existing node ids keep their meaning. A breaking node-id change fails the requirement.

async-opcua was chosen deliberately for RustCrypto over openssl-sys, so the module builds headless on Termux/aarch64-linux-android with no target gate. v3 must not break that.

If adding a SECOND simulator to the shared core, ciet_opcua/mod.rs points at opcua_core::simulator as the thing to read first.
title: CIET v3: OPC-UA server that the EXISTING ciet_v2_opcua_client drives unmodified

description: The schematic's T_fuel tag, reactor-vessel colour, and diagnostics/plot rows read HtgrSnapshot::fuel_temperature_k (the kinetics Nordheim-Fuchs reactivity-feedback node) instead of HtgrSnapshot::bed_temperature_k (the actual PebbleBedPorousMediaNode bed average). The kinetics node has no decay-heat source but is charged the same coolant heat-removal sink as the bed, so after a scram it drifts increasingly colder than the real bed -- measured -10.2 K by 5 sim-minutes post-scram in physics::tests::reproduce_issue_22_kinetics_fuel_node_vs_bed_node_divergence. This produced the apparent second-law violation reported in GitHub issue #22 (T_fuel < T_He,out on screen). Verified the coupled two-phase solve itself is NOT at fault: physics::tests::reproduce_issue_22_scram_cooldown_energy_balance ran a full scram + 30 sim-minute cooldown and found no T_f > T_s inversion (worst case -5.4 K). Fixed by pointing app::schematic and app::panels at bed_temperature_k for anything compared against a helium temperature; fuel_temperature_k remains available (relabelled) for inspecting the reactivity-feedback path itself. Files: examples/htgr_sim_v1/app/{schematic.rs,panels.rs,state.rs}, examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/mod.rs (two new ignored regression tests).

notes.content: Verified fixed. Two regression tests added and green: physics::tests::kinetics_fuel_node_tracks_the_bed_node_after_a_scram (kinetics fuel-node/bed-node gap: -10.2 K before the apply_decay_heat fix, +0.039 K after, 5 sim-min post-scram) and physics::tests::reproduce_issue_22_scram_cooldown_energy_balance (worst T_f-T_s inversion over 30 sim-minutes: -5.4252 K, i.e. no second-law violation in the coupled solve). Full test suite (cargo test --release -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --lib --tests --examples) green: 314 lib + 119 htgr_sim_v1 + 19 fhr_sim_v2 + 21 widget_studio + 3 distillation_sim_v1 + CIET v2 OPC-UA/headless tests, 0 failures. Two fixes landed: (1) app::schematic/app::panels now read bed_temperature_k instead of fuel_temperature_k for anything compared against a helium temperature; (2) HtgrKinetics::apply_decay_heat adds the missing decay-heat source term to the kinetics fuel node, symmetric with its existing coolant-removal sink. Also implemented this session: a fast-forward control (RealTimePacer::set_simulated_per_tick + bounded burst stepping in htgr_sim_v1's physics thread, GUI checkbox in Controls panel).

title: htgr_sim_v1: GUI read the wrong fuel-temperature node (GitHub issue #22)

design:
## What changed

`CLAUDE.md` now gates the "if it is too complex for Haiku, it is a bad API"
rule behind a maturity declaration. Previously it read as binding on *every*
crate in the workspace, which was wrong in both directions: it invited
usability work on crates whose physics is still moving, and gave no signal
about which crates the rule genuinely governs.

## The rule as written

- Hard rule for crates the maintainer has **declared mature**; not enforced
  before that.
- API polish comes **after** the internals are shown reasonably accurate.
  Shaping an interface around moving physics means paying for it twice — the
  wheel, stubs, examples and codegen registry all move with it. An API that
  is pleasant to call and quietly wrong is worse than an awkward one, because
  the ergonomics invite trust the numbers have not earned.
- **Reasonably accurate** = at least one of: analytical/manufactured solution
  (proves the numerics); cross-code comparison against OpenMC/Serpent/MOOSE/
  OpenFOAM/NJOY; or unit tests + conservation/symmetry/limiting-case
  invariants (sufficient alone only for crates with no physics to get wrong).
- **Published-benchmark agreement is deliberately excluded.** HTR-10, MSRE and
  ICSBEP are the *goal* of the validation pipeline, and that pipeline runs
  through the very API in question — requiring it first would deadlock the
  work. Benchmark agreement is the reward for a good API, not its entry fee.
- **Tolerance is per-crate**, declared in that crate's own `CLAUDE.md`, with
  the reference and evidence class named. 500 pcm means something in
  `outram-mc-libs` and nothing in `outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs`. A crate with
  no such statement is by definition not mature.
- **Only the maintainer declares maturity.** An agent may *propose* it — open
  the issue in both trackers, cite specific runs and numbers, stop there.
- **The bar moves.** Revisions are dated entries in the crate's `CLAUDE.md`,
  superseded entries kept, so a later reader does not misread old results as
  failures against a standard that did not exist yet.

## Follow-up work this implies

1. No crate currently carries a maturity declaration, so as of now **zero
   crates are subject to the dogfooding rule**. That is the correct starting
   state, but it means the rule is dormant until the first declaration.
2. Each crate needs a tolerance/reference/evidence line before it can be
   considered. Candidates with the most existing evidence: `outram-mc-libs`
   (Godiva -341 pcm vs ICSBEP), `njoy-outram-park-fork` (RECONR/BROADR vs
   NJOY), `teh-o-prke` (analytical PRKE solutions).
3. The `outram-park` wheel's own dogfood run should state which crates it
   covers, rather than implying all 36.
title: Gate the Haiku API-dogfooding rule behind a per-crate maturity declaration
